full_judgment: 11. By taking this Court through the provisions of Section 38 of the Companies Act, Mr Badrudduza submits that the law contemplates that it shall not be lawful to register transfer of shares without proper instrument of transfer having stamped with required amount of fees, if the same are not executed by the transferor and the transferee, and if the scripts of the share certificates have not been delivered to the company. He argues that since in the instant case, respondent Nos. 2-6 have failed to produce any duly stamped proper instrument of transfer signed by the transferor and the transferee, and since the original scripts are lying with petitioner Nos.1 and 2, this Court should declare that petitioner Nos. 1 and 2 are the lawful owners of the shares in question. By placing Section 43( I )(a) of the Companies Act, Mr Badruddoza submits that the law clearly stipulates that this Court is empowered to rectify the company's Register of Members if the name of any person is without sufficient cause entered in or omitted from the Register of Members of a company and, since in the instant case, there was no sufficient cause to enter the names of respondent Nos. 2-6 in the Register of Members as no Board resolution, proper instrument of transfer duly stamped and signed by the transferor and transferee along with scripts could be produced before this Court, there has not been any transfer of shares on 7-3-2011 by petitioner to the respondent Nos. 2-6. Mr Badrudduza further argues that since respondent Nos. 2-6 did not specifically challenge the signatures of their father to have been forged by petitioner No. 1, nor did make any prayer for expert opinion, as such, they have no right to seek reversal of the transfer of shares held on 15-7-2000 and 15-11-2000. He further argues that since the respondent Nos. 2-6 did not apply to this Court for rectification of the Register of Members, they are debarred to seek such relief in a case filed by petitioners for omission of their names from the Register. In support his submissions, he refers to the case of Jabed Ali vs Dr Sultan Ahmed, 26 DLR 303 and the case of Mankji Pestonji Bharncha vs Wadilal Sarabhai & Co., 30 CWN (PC) 890.
